About Us
Chutney Bar Mornington is a well-established Indian restaurant located in the heart of Mornington on the Mornington Peninsula. We are renowned for serving authentic North and South Indian cuisine prepared using traditional recipes, premium-quality ingredients, aromatic spices, and modern cooking techniques. Our extensive menu features a variety of curries, tandoori specialties, biryanis, vegetarian dishes, breads, and regional delicacies, catering to both dine-in and takeaway customers.

•	Prepare ingredients by washing, peeling, cutting, marinating and measuring food items prior to cooking.

•	Ensure all dishes are prepared and presented in accordance with the restaurant's quality standards and customer expectations. 
•	Monitor cooking times, temperatures and portion sizes to maintain consistency and minimise food wastage. 
•	Check the quality and freshness of meat, seafood, vegetables, spices and other ingredients before use and report any quality concerns. 
•	Store food safely in accordance with food safety regulations and maintain appropriate stock rotation using FIFO principles.

•	Maintain cleanliness and sanitation of kitchen equipment, food preparation areas and storage facilities in compliance with Food Safety Standards Australia New Zealand (FSANZ) and workplace health and safety requirements. 
•	Follow safe food handling practices and ensure compliance with hygiene regulations at all times. 
•	Work efficiently during busy service periods to ensure timely preparation and service of meals. 
•	Assist in preparing meals for customers with dietary requirements or food allergies while maintaining quality and presentation standards. 
•	Collaborate effectively with chefs, cooks and front-of-house staff to ensure smooth kitchen operations and excellent customer service. 
•	Assist with the preparation of daily specials and seasonal menu items under the direction of senior kitchen staff. 
•	Operate commercial kitchen equipment safely and report any maintenance issues promptly. 
To be Successful in this Role, You Will Have
•	Certificate III or Certificate IV in Commercial Cookery, or an equivalent recognised qualification. 
•	Minimum two years' experience as a Cook in a busy commercial kitchen, preferably specialising in authentic Indian cuisine. 
•	Demonstrated knowledge of Indian spices, herbs, marinades, traditional cooking methods and tandoor cooking techniques. 
•	Sound understanding of food safety, hygiene and workplace health and safety regulations. 
•	Ability to prepare high-quality meals efficiently in a fast-paced restaurant environment. 
•	Strong organisational skills with the ability to prioritise multiple tasks during busy service periods. 
•	Excellent teamwork and communication skills. 
•	Flexibility to work weekends, evenings and public holidays as required. 
Join Chutney Bar Mornington, where tradition, taste, and teamwork come together to create memorable dining experiences.
We look forward to welcoming a passionate and dedicated Cook to join our kitchen team and contribute to delivering authentic, high-quality dining experiences for our customers.

At Mushroom People Pty Ltd, we are a proud family-owned and operated gourmet mushroom farm located on the west side of Melbourne. Our deep passion for seeing mushrooms grow and staying connected to nature is at the heart of everything we do. We believe in sustainable, environmentally friendly farming practices that look after our local community and promote a healthier planet. Every single one of our gourmet varieties (including exotic Oyster and Lion's Mane varieties) is grown with love and delivered fresh to restaurants, grocery stores, and wholesalers across Australia.

As we expand our production, we are looking for a dedicated full-time Horticultural Grower (Mushroom Grower) (working 38 hours per week) to join our tight-knit farm family and help us grow with love.

The base salary offered is 79,500 - 82,500 per annum plus superannuation.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

- Planning and coordinating the cultivation, production, and marketing of gourmet mushroom crops from initial substrate preparation to final harvest, taking into careful account environmental variables and shifting market factors.
- Selecting, preparing, and inoculating grain spawn and liquid cultures, while grafting and testing new exotic mushroom strains to optimize crop resilience and yield.
- Maintaining optimal indoor crop production cycles by cultivating mycelium blocks, de-budding excess pinheads, monitoring flushing intervals, and adjusting climate control infrastructure.
- Organising and conducting daily commercial farming operations, including the strategic collecting, cold storage, strict grading, and eco-friendly packaging of fresh gourmet produce.
- Directing the sale, purchase, and dispatch of mushroom products to local wholesalers, restaurants, and grocery networks to meet tight delivery contracts.
- Overseeing general bio-secure farming activities, with a strict focus on non-chemical pest management, pathogen controls, and rigorous environmental hygiene.
- Maintaining facility infrastructure, specialised climate incubation rooms, commercial vertical shelf equipment, and automated water-misting supply systems.
- Evaluating comprehensive records of all farming activities, tracking market price fluctuations, and forecasting crop preparation volumes to meet seasonal consumer demand.
- Managing crop production within established budgets, tracking operational expenses, and reporting financial performance to business owners.
- Selecting, hiring, training, and supervising diverse farm staff and contractors to ensure total alignment with the farm's sustainable, family-oriented operational ethos.
- Overseeing climate and humidity controls within the grow rooms to protect crops from external weather fluctuations and ensure stable, year-round yields.
- Managing strict workplace health and safety (WHS) processes, while ensuring continuous facility compliance with Freshcare and HARPS food safety standards for exotic mushroom production.

Skills, Qualifications and Experience Required

- At least an AQF Certificate III or IV in Horticulture, Agriculture, or Agribusiness (Alternatively, at least 5 years of relevant work experience may be substituted for the degree).
- Minimum of 2 years of relevant work experience in a supervisory or management role within an intensive primary production, commercial horticultural, or indoor cultivation environment.
- Strong knowledge and practical experience in agricultural production principles, specifically including indoor climate control, substrate handling, and crop hygiene.
- Demonstrated experience working within commercial food safety frameworks, with exposure to Freshcare and HARPS compliance and audit readiness highly regarded.
- Excellent communication, team leadership, and organisational skills, with a proven ability to manage daily tasks, lead a small production team, and meet strict harvesting and delivery deadlines.
